caseAnalysis.title: Camp Alpha Commander and FWB Food Distribution Negotiation
caseAnalysis.summary: The role card represents the Camp Alpha commander, who is negotiating with Food Without Borders (FWB) over food aid for 160,000 refugees held by about 700 guards. According to the camp-side minutes, FWB refuses to feed guards, wants FWB-managed distribution and requests nutritional assessments for a donor requirement. The camp side wants distribution to run through guard structures, with FWB presence escorted. The commander pays guards partly with diverted refugee food. Guards may rebel if they see refugees eat better than they do. The government expects refugees kept out of the capital. Officials say major unrest or visible abuse would be politically costly. SML, the Mayor's Office and others add pressures. SML demands that militia be involved and compensated, and condones threats and skimming. Fuel payments and generators are failing. The role card describes confiscation by force as possible, but it would end future aid and risk foreign troops.
caseAnalysis.objective: Reach an agreement with FWB that includes ongoing food aid, helps sustain guards and keep refugees in the camp, and preserves the commander's authority and stability without major unrest or visible abuse.
caseAnalysis.outside_option: The role card describes disengaging from FWB to pressure the Ministry of Health for rations and the Ministry of Defense for funds. Whether either would deliver is unconfirmed.

red_lines.text: Keep refugees in the camp, per the government's expectation.

issues.text: SML's 'take the food' is ambiguous: it could mean accepting the aid or seizing it.
FWB's donor requirement for an assessment is reported only, and the camp-side authors doubt it.
SML's stated plans to skim food and distribute unequally conflict with the political cost of visible abuse.

immediate.text: A new FWB negotiator is reaching out. According to the camp-side minutes, the prior meeting stalled over guard food, control of distribution and assessments.

actors.text: FWB, as reported, refuses to feed guards and wants FWB-managed disbursement.
SML demands that militia be involved in and compensated for distribution, and wants this settled before FWB arrives.
The Mayor's Office wants camp-linked local jobs and income protected, local actors prioritized and stability maintained.
Guards are unpaid or underpaid and may rebel if refugees eat better than they do.
MASHA has a working relationship with camp administration, and its access clears through Camp Admin. The commander has had narrative problems with MASHA.

tension.text: The camp needs the food and wants it to sustain guards, but FWB rejects feeding guards on neutrality grounds and wants independent control.

background.text: The commander has kept guards by diverting refugee food because corruption leaves salaries unpaid. The generator is failing and fuel has not been paid for weeks.

uncertainty.text: It is unclear whether FWB's donor assessment requirement is firm.
The commander suspects JJP and the ministries may have more resources than they disclose. This is unverified.
Whether SML's guaranteed payment arrives next week is uncertain. The same promise was reportedly made the previous week.

fallback.text: Proposed fallback: keep ongoing aid flowing by accepting FWB oversight of refugee rations. Pursue guard sustenance separately through the Ministries rather than diverting refugee food.

alternatives.text: Disengage and press the Ministry of Health and Ministry of Defense for rations and funds. Their capacity is unconfirmed.
Offer existing registration data as a partial input to FWB's assessment, to reduce security exposure and delay.

response_branches.text: If FWB holds firm on no food for guards, explore whether FWB-supported local employment can be framed as wages rather than diverted aid. Verify this with FWB before relying on it.
If FWB insists on independently hired assistants, discuss vetting and escort arrangements to address the authority and unrest concerns.
If FWB treats the assessment as mandatory for its donor, ask for a scoped, escorted, phased assessment.

Guard discipline can be sustained by sources other than refugee rations.
SML will tolerate an arrangement that does not meet its full demands.

background.text: Some refugees trade rations for essentials, and the rations are resold locally.
The petrol supplier agreed to deliver after the commander requested one more week to pay.

people_interests_power.text: The commander fears SML would send a hitman if SML thinks he is going to crack.
